history.dynasty: Mewar (Sisodia, Rana Kumbha period); commissioned by the Porwal Jain minister Dharna Shah (Dhanna Shah)
history.period: 15th century (construction began 1439 AD under Rana Kumbha; took about 65 years to complete)
history.summary: TRADITION FLAG: this is a JAIN temple (Śvetāmbara), not a Hindu one. The 'Adishwar Temple, Pali' of the CSV is the famous Chaumukha (four-faced) Temple at Ranakpur: every detail in the sources (15th century, 65 years' construction, 3 storeys, 80 domes, 29 halls, 1444 pillars, Nalinigulm Vimana, four-faced Adinath/Rishabhdev) matches Ranakpur, not a separate site. Legend holds that Dharna Shah, a Porwal Jain minister, dreamed of a celestial palace (Nalinigulm Vimana) and commissioned the temple with Rana Kumbha's patronage (condition: it be named after the king). The 6-ft chaumukha idol of Adinath sits in the garbhagriha; the 1444 carved marble pillars are all unique, the complex has 84 underground bhonyra chambers, and the Parshvanatha shrine's 1008-snake-head idol is famed. One of the five major Jain pilgrimage centres of India; ASI-protected. CSV TOWN FLAG: it is NOT in Pali city - it stands at Ranakpur in Desuri tehsil, about 90 km from Pali city. name: Adishwar Temple (Ranakpur Chaumukha Temple)
town: Ranakpur, Desuri tehsil (CSV town 'Pali' is wrong - the temple is at Ranakpur, ~90 km from Pali city)
town_description: Ranakpur is a small village in Desuri tehsil of Pali district, nestled in a quiet valley of the Aravalli Range on the banks of the Maghai (Mavi) river. It is one of India's great Jain pilgrimage centres, surrounded by forested hills; the nearest railhead is Falna and the nearest airports are Udaipur and Jodhpur.

travel.airport: Udaipur Airport - about 90-100 km; Jodhpur Airport - about 150 km (verify).
travel.railway: Falna railway station - about 35 km; taxi/bus onward.
travel.road: On the Jodhpur-Udaipur highway via Sadri/Desuri; buses and taxis from Falna, Udaipur, and Jodhpur.

visitor_information.opening_hours: Jain temple: typically 12:00 noon - 5:00 pm for non-Jain visitors (verify - confirm locally); photography fees and leather/mobile restrictions apply inside the complex.
